raw:
The literature results are unrelated to NAS-Bench-201 (power grids, transistors, a particle spectrometer), so these hypotheses rest on what I know of the benchmark rather than on them. I haven't run any experiments, so each one is a prior I expect to hold, not a measured result.

Reasoning behind the choices:
- Edge 2 (1->2) is the second hop of the 0->1->2 chain. When the parallel direct edge 1 (0->2) is skip_connect, there is already a clean gradient path, so the extra conv on edge 2 adds less. When edge 1 is none, edge 2 is the only route into node 2, so a conv there matters more.
- Upgrading to conv matters most when it replaces a weak op. Replacing none or avg_pool gains more than replacing skip_connect or a conv.
- Stacked avg_pool_3x3 on consecutive hops oversmooths features, so pooling on edge 4 or 5 hurts more when the upstream edge 0 or 2 is also pooling.
- At output node 3, convs on parallel branches are largely substitutes, so a second conv adds less once another branch already has one.
